question: The world’s oldest first-class cricketer and World War II veteran, Alan Burgess passed away in January 2021. He represented which of the following countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Zealand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Alan Burgess was a former New Zealand cricketer**__.

 __
 
• He played first-class cricket for Canterbury from 1940 to 1952.
 
• During **World War II,** he served as a tank driver.
 
• He joined the New Zealand Army in 1941.
 
• In 1944, he took part in the** Battle of Monte Cassino.**
 
• He toured England with the New Zealand Services team as a batsman after the war in Europe finished.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Alan Burgess was the **world's oldest living first-class cricketer**.

 
 
• He passed away in **January 2021.**
 
• When Tom Pritchard died in August 2017, Alan Burgess became** New Zealand's oldest living first-class cricketer.**
 
• Burgess became the oldest living first-class cricketer on June 13, 2020, when **Vasant Raiji died.**
 
 
 
• Following Burgess' death, **Raghunath Chandorkar** of India became the world's oldest living first-class cricketer, while** Iain Gallaway** of New Zealand became the world's oldest living first-class cricketer.
